I'm working in the Nxeon codebase at /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma hosting platform). The owner wants paid Minecraft game-server customers to be able to connect via a subdomain (e.g. `bujangsmp.play.nxeon.cloud` or similar) instead of a raw IP:port — this matters especially for customers without a dedicated IP, where the connect string is an ugly `sharedPublicIp:forwardedPort`.

I need you to research and report back (no edits, research only):

1. **The existing free Minecraft tier's subdomain routing** — per my notes this already exists: a `freemc-host` VM + Docker + `mc-router` giving subdomain-based routing with auto-sleep/wake, similar to Aternos. Find this code (likely `worker/` or a dedicated file/dir — grep for "mc-router", "freemc", "mcrouter"). Document exactly how it works: what DNS is involved (wildcard DNS record? per-server record creation?), how `mc-router` maps an incoming hostname to the right backend container/port, whether it uses Minecraft's SRV-record mechanism or just a wildcard `*.something.nxeon.cloud` A record + mc-router's hostname-based proxying (which works because Minecraft's handshake packet includes the hostname the client typed, so a single IP:25565 can host many named subdomains behind one router). Read the actual source.

2. **Whether this mc-router infrastructure could be reused for PAID game servers**, or whether it's structurally free-tier-only (e.g. hardcoded to one shared VM, one Docker network, assumes containers are colocated). Paid Minecraft servers each run in their OWN separate Proxmox VM (see worker/index.ts's provision()), often with their own dedicated IP OR a shared-IP+forwarded-port setup — check whether mc-router's approach (single shared IP:25565, route by hostname) is even compatible with that model, or whether paid servers would need a different approach (e.g. a real SRV DNS record per server, `_minecraft._tcp.<subdomain>.nxeon.cloud` pointing at `host:port`, since Minecraft clients honor SRV records to let you type a bare domain instead of domain:port).

3. **Existing DNS-provider integration** — how does Nxeon manage DNS records it controls today for its OWN domains (nxeon.cloud, nxeon.gg, whatever they use)? Check `lib/registrar.ts`, `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts`, and search for any Cloudflare API usage, or any existing internal DNS zone management (e.g. for mail.nxeon.cloud, the free-MC subdomains, or wildcard cert issuance in `worker/ssl.ts`). Report exactly which DNS API/provider is used for records Nxeon creates on its own domains, and whether there's already a reusable helper function for "create a DNS record programmatically" I could call from the game-server provisioning worker.

4. **The `Server` and `GamePlan`/`OsTemplate` Prisma models** — check `prisma/schema.prisma` for any existing subdomain-related field on `Server` (grep "subdomain", "customDomain", "fqdn", "hostname" near game-related fields). Also check if VPS-style websites (`worker/websites.ts`, `worker/site-publish.ts`) already have a "give this a Nxeon subdomain" pattern I could mirror (many hosting platforms give free `*.customerproject.nxeon.cloud`-style subdomains to new sites) — if so, that's a strong existing pattern to reuse for game servers.

5. **The actual customer-facing "Network"/"Connect" UI** — `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`'s game branch (`gameSettingsPanel`, around line 987-1037 as of now, look for the "Network" card) currently shows only the raw `connect` string (`ip:port`). Note this so I know exactly what UI would need to change to show/manage a subdomain instead of or alongside the IP.

Report back concisely but completely: what already exists and is reusable, what's free-tier-only and NOT reusable as-is, and what a paid-tier subdomain feature would need to build from scratch (DNS record creation at provision time, whether SRV records or wildcard+router is the right mechanism given paid servers are NOT colocated on one shared VM, and where in worker/index.ts's provision() flow a DNS-record-creation step would need to be added). This is purely investigative — do not write any code.

## Summary of Findings ### 1. Free-tier Minecraft subdomain routing — how it actually works Core files: - `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts` (1049 lines) — Docker/RCON primitives for containers on `freemc-host` - `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts` — server actions (create/rename/subdomain-change/etc.) - `prisma/schema.prisma` `model FreeMinecraftServer` (~line 2327) **Mechanism (confirmed from source, not docs):** - One shared Docker host, VM identified in the DB as `Server.hostname === "freemc-host"` (a real internal `Server` row, looked up via `freemcHost()` in `actions-free-minecraft.ts:63-73`). - All containers run on a shared Docker network (`--network freemc`) on that single host, each started with `itzg/minecraft-server` and labeled `--label mc-router.host=.` (`free-minecraft-control.ts:908`). `mc-router` (itzg's Go proxy, a pre-existing binary/container **not present in this repo at all** — it's deployed once on the host as external infra, never referenced by any docker-compose or setup script in the codebase) reads Docker labels, sees the hostname the Minecraft client sent in its handshake packet, and proxies the TCP connection to the matching container's `25565`. This is exactly the mechanism the user described: one shared `IP:25565`, hostname-based routing off Minecraft's own handshake field — **not** SRV records. - DNS is a **single static wildcard** — `getSetting("free_minecraft_domain", "play.nxeon.cloud")` is a fixed platform setting (`lib/actions-settings.ts:265`), and grepping every call site (`changeFreeMinecraftSubdomain` in `actions-free-minecraft.ts:323-380`, world/mod actions) shows **zero DNS API calls anywhere in this flow**. Renaming a subdomain only updates the DB row + recreates the container with a new label — it never touches DNS, because `*.play.nxeon.cloud` already resolves (presumably a wildcard A record pointing at freemc-host's IP, set up once, out-of-band, not in this codebase). `mc-router` does all the per-subdomain "routing," DNS does none of it. - Auto-sleep/wake is entirely `mc-router`'s own feature (`-auto-scale-down-after`, referenced in `actions-settings.ts:272` and `freemc-capacity.ts`'s module doc) — nothing in this app drives it. ### 2. Is this reusable for paid servers? No — structurally free-tier-only This is the key finding, and the code itself proves it: - `mc-router`'s whole trick only works because every free container is **colocated on one host, sharing one public IP and port 25565**. Paid Minecraft servers are each their **own separate Proxmox VM** (`worker/index.ts`'s `provision()`), with either a real `DedicatedIp` (own unique public IP, from an OVH block — `model DedicatedIp` in schema.prisma) or a shared NAT node IP + a per-server `PortForward` row (`publicPort -> guestPort`, created only when the customer manually adds one via `lib/actions-server.ts:298`, confirmed by the comment in `worker/index.ts:677-678`: *"a game's own port is forwarded only if the customer adds one... a separate pre-existing gap"*). - A wildcard `*.paid.nxeon.cloud` A record pointing at one IP is meaningless once every server lives at a **different** IP (or the same shared NAT IP but a **different port**). `mc-router` has no way to route by port, only by hostname within one shared listener — it cannot solve "same hostname family, different backend IP:port per customer." - Conclusion: none of `free-minecraft-control.ts`'s container/label/`mc-router` machinery is reusable. Paid servers need a **per-server DNS record**, not a shared wildcard + router. ### 3. Existing DNS-provider integration Two separate, unrelated DNS surfaces exist: - **`lib/registrar.ts`** — name.com reseller API client (`nc()` helper, `NAMECOM_USERNAME`/`NAMECOM_TOKEN` env vars). Exposes fully generic, reusable helpers already used for customer-purchased domains: ```ts listRecords(domain): Promise addRecord(domain, { host, type, answer, ttl?, priority? }): Promise // registrar.ts:606 deleteRecord(domain, id): Promise ``` `RECORD_TYPES` in the calling layer (`lib/actions-domains-dns.ts:60`, `lib/actions-domains.ts:775`) already includes `"SRV"` and passes `priority` for it — **SRV creation is already plumbed through this API**, just currently only exposed to customers managing their *own* registered domain. - **`lib/cloudflare-dns.ts`** — a separate Cloudflare v4 client, but it's for **customer-supplied Cloudflare API tokens** (connecting a customer's own Cloudflare-hosted domain), and its `CfRecordType` union is only `"TXT" | "MX" | "A"` — no SRV/CNAME support, and it takes a per-call customer token, not a platform-owned one. - **Nxeon's own domain(s)** (`nxeon.cloud`, `play.nxeon.cloud`, `nxeon.site` for the site builder): I found **no code anywhere** that programmatically manages Nxeon's own zone. No `Domain` row, no "platform domain" flag, no internal DNS helper call for `play.nxeon.cloud` or `nxeon.site`. The wildcard records these subdomains depend on were set up manually/out-of-band. There is currently **no reusable "create a DNS record on our own domain" helper** — `registrar.ts`'s `addRecord()` is reusable *in principle* (generic name.com API wrapper) **only if** `nxeon.cloud` is itself registered/managed through the same name.com reseller account Nxeon uses for customer domains — that needs to be confirmed operationally, since the codebase gives no evidence either way. ### 4. Schema fields & the site-builder subdomain pattern - `Server` model: **no** `subdomain`/`customDomain`/`fqdn` field exists for game servers. `GamePlan`/`OsTemplate` likewise have nothing DNS-related. - `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` is the only game-adjacent subdomain field, and it's fully decoupled from `Server`. - **Strong reusable pattern**: `worker/site-publish.ts` (Website Builder) does effectively the same thing as freemc, for websites: every Site publishes to `.nxeon.site` (`BASE_DOMAIN = process.env.SITE_BUILDER_BASE_DOMAIN || "nxeon.site"`, `publishDomain()` at line 66) on **one shared builder host** (`BUILDER_SERVER_ID`), reusing `worker/websites.ts`'s nginx vhost machinery. Same shape as freemc: single shared host + wildcard DNS + hostname-based reverse proxy (nginx here, `mc-router` there) — **also not reusable as-is** for the same reason: paid game servers aren't colocated on one shared host/IP. - There's also `NxCloudInstance.subdomain` (`.nxcloud.nxeon.cloud`, schema.prisma ~line 4845-4848) — another instance of the same "shared host + wildcard + subdomain label" pattern, again not per-VM. - **Net finding**: every existing "give a Nxeon subdomain" pattern in this codebase (freemc, site builder, NxCloud) assumes one shared backing host per wildcard domain. None of them is a template for "one DNS record per independently-hosted VM," which is what paid game servers need. ### 5. Customer-facing Network/Connect UI `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`: - `connect` string built at lines 950-954: ```ts const connect = server.dedicatedIp ? `${server.dedicatedIp.address}${gameForward ? `:${gameForward.guestPort}` : ""}` : gameForward ? `${publicIp}:${gameForward.publicPort}` : publicIp || null; ``` - Rendered in the "Network" card at lines 1028-1035, literally just: ```tsx

Network

Your server connects on:

{connect ?? "provisioning…"}
``` This is the exact spot that would need to change to show a subdomain (in place of, or alongside, the raw `ip:port`). ### What a paid-tier subdomain feature would need to build from scratch 1. **DNS mechanism**: given paid servers are NOT colocated, the wildcard+`mc-router` approach is not viable. The right mechanism is almost certainly a real **SRV record per server** — `_minecraft._tcp..nxeon.cloud` → `:` — which Minecraft Java clients already honor (this needs zero backend routing infra, unlike `mc-router`, since each SRV record just points straight at that server's own dedicated IP or NAT-IP+forwardedPort). This is the standard way to give a bare, port-free domain to a service that's on its own dedicated host+port, and it maps cleanly onto Nxeon's existing per-server `DedicatedIp`/`PortForward` model. 2. **Schema**: add a `subdomain` (or `fqdn`) field to `Server` (or a small companion model, mirroring `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain`'s uniqueness/validation pattern) plus maybe a `dnsRecordId`/`dnsSynced` bookkeeping field. 3. **DNS API call**: `lib/registrar.ts`'s `addRecord()`/`deleteRecord()` (name.com) is the closest existing reusable primitive — generic, already used for SRV elsewhere — but it needs to be pointed at Nxeon's own domain, which currently has no established code path; this would need to be newly wired (confirm nxeon.cloud is on the same name.com account, or otherwise pick/build a provider client for Nxeon's own zone). 4. **Provisioning integration point**: in `worker/index.ts`'s `provision()`, the natural insertion point is **right after the game-port-open check succeeds** (around line 690, before `status: "RUNNING"` is set at line 704) — that's the first point where the final `ip`/`dedicated`/game port are all confirmed live and correct. A DNS-record-creation step (SRV pointing at `ip:port`, or `ip:sshCheckPort`-equivalent for the game port) should go there, gated the same way the rest of `provision()` gates on `SANDBOX`, with the same "never fake success" discipline used elsewhere in that function. 5. **UI**: update the `connect` computation and the "Network" card (`app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx:950-1035`) to prefer/show the subdomain once a DNS record exists, falling back to the raw `ip:port` otherwise (matching how `freemc`'s dashboard shows the subdomain today).
